thread:
maria: CI linkcheck failing on latest deploy, reproducible locally. it marks several in-page anchors as missing even though they exist visually in the HTML :confused:
ben: can you paste the exact linkcheck lines from the action log?
maria: pasted below:
```
LinkCheck: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/usage#installing-the-sdk -> 404 (fragment not found)
LinkCheck: https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/model-routing#route-priorities -> 404 (fragment mismatch)
```
ben: looks like a slug mismatch. any strange characters in those headings?
maria: yes — one heading has inline code `--prefer-quantization`, another ends with an emoji :gear:. slug generation likely differs between authorship and the renderer.
oliver: this matches fallout from the mkdocs -> docusaurus migration. Docusaurus's slugify normalizer treats inline code and emoji differently than the old pipeline. saw a few similar reports.
ben: short-term workaround: authors can add explicit heading ids like `### Installing the SDK {#installing-the-sdk}` or change heading text to a plain phrase. long-term we should normalize slug generation across the build.
celine: I can open a small PR adding a remark/rehype plugin to canonicalize heading ids: strip emoji, collapse inline code tokens into plain text, and ensure consistent ASCII folding. want me to draft it?
maria: please do. also can we add a temporary linkcheck allowlist for known redirect/normalize cases so CI noise is reduced while we ship the slugifier?
ben: +1 on allowlist, but prefer fixing canonical slugger first. celine, if you draft the plugin I'll add tests. in the meantime I'll fix the three docs that keep failing.
docs-bot: Deploy preview for PR #4328 is live at https://deploy-preview-4328--docs.redwood.ai/ :eyes:
oliver: celine, make sure the plugin runs the same normalization for both generated heading ids and for resolving explicit reference anchors (`[foo](#bar)`) so authors don't get surprises. also include compatibility for existing explicit `{#id}` if present.
celine: good note. I'll add unit tests: a small suite of markdown cases with inline code, emoji, smart quotes, and non-ascii. also will add a local `scripts/slugcheck.js` that compares generated anchors vs all link refs and fails on mismatches. will wire that into a GH Action step.
maria: if it helps, I can open a hotfix PR updating the immediate pages: `docs/sdk/getting-started.md`, `docs/guides/model-routing.md`, `docs/ops/latency-tuning.md` to use explicit ids. PR title: "docs: temp fix broken fragment links" — assign to ben.
ben: taking review. i'll also add a note in docs/CONTRIBUTING.md recommending explicit ids for headings with inline code until slugifier is merged.
oliver: small UX idea: make the preview bot include direct fragment links in its PR comment so reviewers can jump straight to the anchor on the deploy preview. tiny but useful.
docs-bot: Updated PR comment on #4329 with direct fragment anchors for quick review.
celine: I'll open the slugifier draft today and tag you all. will include migration notes and a rollback toggle in the build config.
maria: thanks — i'll watch CI and post back if anything else surfaces. :thumbsup:
ben: cool. once slugifier lands, we can revert the hotfix edits and remove the allowlist.
(maria edited message)
